notes.summary: Draft bounded C_theta integration by parts, first variation, concavity, tangent inequality and comparison. Uses local ordinary smooth-positive approximants, without a global positive approximation theorem.
notes.detailedSummary: On compact good separated smooth boundaryless analytic surfaces, coefficient Radon control and fixed-current Dirichlet estimates establish integration by parts for the entire specified bounded class. Consequently E'(u_t)=integral(v-u)MA(u_t), E''(u_t)<=0, and the tangent inequality holds for every bounded competitor. Finite-max locality and conserved mass also give bounded comparison. The argument retains published CLD infrastructure and does not establish an all-direction unbounded E1 theory.
notes.text:
This is an unverified proof draft.

Let X be a compact, good, separated, smooth, boundaryless analytic surface with canonical CLD integration. Let theta be a smooth positive closed (1,1)-form with local smooth positive potentials q. Define C_theta to consist of continuous u such that, on an ordinary neighborhood of each point, q+u is a locally uniform limit of ordinary smooth functions with middle-positive Hessian. Write DD=d'd'', alpha_u=theta+DD[u], and V=integral theta^2.

The published infrastructure used is CLD arXiv:1204.6277v2, 25 July 2025: ordinary smooth cutoffs and finite partitions, positive-current coefficient representation and continuous multiplication, canonical integration, and smooth closed-factor calculus. Applied units are 6.5.2, 7.2.8/11/13, 7.7.1-8, 8.5.1/3/5, 8.7.1/2/4 and 15.7.1-2. Their goodness, separation, pure-dimension and boundary hypotheses are retained. No general continuous-multiplier closedness assertion is used.

First construct the bounded products. In a moment presentation, symmetric coefficient forms correspond to symmetric matrices on an exterior coefficient space. The middle-positive cone is PSD, and the appropriate power of a Euclidean positive form is a positive multiple of the identity. A cutoff therefore bounds any compact symmetric test above and below by middle-positive tests. Positivity gives coefficient Radon measures through Riesz representation. If positive T_i converge weakly and b_i converge locally uniformly, then b_i T_i converge to bT: approximate b uniformly on the test support by a smooth scalar g and split the difference into (b_i-g)T_i+g(T_i-T)+(g-b)T. Positive test masses bound the error terms.

Locally put p=q+u, r=q+v and B(u,v)=DD(p DD[r]). Simultaneous smooth positive approximants and the preceding multiplication estimate show that this is the weak limit of positive smooth mixed products. It is positive, symmetric, local, independent of approximants and continuous for locally uniform convergence in the declared class. Smooth DD-null changes of q glue it. Globally
B(u,v)=theta wedge alpha_v+DD(u alpha_v),
theta wedge alpha_v=theta^2+DD(v theta).
Testing with 1 gives integral B(u,v)=V. Finite convex combinations and finite maxima belong to C_theta, using common local neighborhoods and smooth convex nondecreasing regularizations. This requires no global positive approximant.

Here is the needed integration by parts. Fix a positive symmetric closed (1,1)-current T; do not approximate T. Locally let f be a difference of two uniformly smooth-positive-approximable weights and choose smooth differences f_i=p_i-r_i converging uniformly on compact subsets. The signed Radon measure L_T f=DD(fT) is the difference of DD(pT) and DD(rT), both positive. For a nonnegative compact smooth cutoff chi,
integral chi DD p_i wedge T=integral p_i DD chi wedge T.
Local uniform bounds on p_i give a uniform mass bound. The same holds for r_i and hence for the signed variations of L_T f_i. Distributional convergence and coefficient multiplication yield L_T f_i -> L_T f and f_i L_T f_i -> f L_T f.

For smooth a define Q_T(a)=d'a wedge d''a wedge T. This is positive and its polarization is symmetric. Smooth closed-factor Leibniz gives
Q_T(a)=(1/2)DD(a^2T)-a L_T a.
For a=f_i-f_j, with uniform error eta on a neighborhood of the cutoff support, the preceding variation bounds give
0<=integral chi Q_T(f_i-f_j)<=C_chi(eta+eta^2).
The same identity bounds integral chi Q_T(f_i) uniformly. PSD coefficient positivity gives Cauchy-Schwarz when d''a wedge T is tested against any compact smooth (1,0)-form beta. This follows by integrating the nonnegative quadratic obtained from lambda beta+d'a; bounded smooth scalar multiples of beta are allowed.

Thus d''f_i wedge T are Cauchy as currents. For another such difference g, the currents f_i d''g_i wedge T are Cauchy: split their difference into (f_i-f_j)d''g_i wedge T and f_j d''(g_i-g_j) wedge T. The first tends to zero by uniform convergence and bounded gradient mass, and the second by the Dirichlet estimate. Interleaving sequences proves independence, including independence of different local difference presentations. The limiting currents glue on overlaps.

For smooth f_i,g_i symmetry cancels cross terms:
d'(f_i d''g_i wedge T-g_i d''f_i wedge T)=f_i L_T g_i-g_i L_T f_i.
Pass to the established local limits and glue. On compact X, testing with 1 proves
integral f DD(gT)=integral g DD(fT).
The positive local limits Q_T(f_i) equal
Q_T(f)=(1/2)DD(f^2T)-f DD(fT),
so integral f DD(fT)=-integral Q_T(f)<=0. Here f^2T is only a coefficient product; it is not asserted closed, and f^2 is not asserted psh. This avoids CLD 8.6.7's continuous-multiplier closedness issue.

Every u in C_theta is locally (q+u)-q. The identities therefore apply to global u,v and to T=theta or alpha_w. Directly from the reconstructed products,
DD((u-v)alpha_w)=B(u,w)-B(v,w).

Define
E(u)=(1/3)integral u(theta^2+theta wedge alpha_u+B(u,u)).
Constants satisfy E(u+C)=E(u)+VC. For f=v-u, u_t=u+tf and alpha_t=alpha_{u_t}, multilinearity makes E(u_t) a polynomial of degree at most three. Differentiation and the proved integration by parts give
E'(u_t)=(1/3)integral f[theta^2+theta alpha_t+alpha_t^2+(alpha_t-theta)(theta+2alpha_t)]
=integral f alpha_t^2.
Differentiating again gives
E''(u_t)=2integral f DD(f alpha_t)=-2integral Q_{alpha_t}(f)<=0.
Integrating the decreasing derivative proves, for EVERY u,v in C_theta,
E(v)<=E(u)+integral(v-u)MA(u).

Comparison also holds for the entire bounded class. For epsilon>0 set w=max(u,v-epsilon). Locality on the two strict open regions and positivity imply
V>=integral_{u>v-epsilon}MA(u)+integral_{u<v-epsilon}MA(v).
Consequently integral_{u<v-epsilon}MA(v)<=integral_{u<=v-epsilon}MA(u). Both sets increase to {u<v} as epsilon decreases to zero. Continuity from below proves integral_{u<v}MA(v)<=integral_{u<v}MA(u). Equality-set mass is correctly included on the intermediate right side.

This proves the bounded variation, concavity, tangent and comparison gates under the named analytic infrastructure. It does not prove unbounded decreasing continuity or intrinsic all-direction E1 recognition.

Complete artifacts: n1.md, P16.7-bounded-dual-paper.tex, proof-companion.md and source-application-ledger.md. Rerun own integrity and finite algebra diagnostics with python identity_audit.py and python diagnostics.py; neither execution establishes this universal analytic proof.

notes.summary: Reconstructed quotient foundation and genuine finite radial MA formulas, with raw mass two. Deep published descent/flatness foundations remain explicit; their entire recursive source audit is incomplete.
notes.detailedSummary: Retains K=C((s)), |s|=exp(-1/8), periods(s^8,2),(3,s^8), and the good strict smooth proper boundaryless connected surface. Disc/circle Gruson, determinant cancellation, rational annulus filling, compatible frames, signed Laurent recurrences and intrinsic pole ideals provide the nonalgebraization argument under named published foundations. Calibrated convex approximants and actual Ducros 2012 Theorem 3.4 give MA(u_h)=(2-c^2)delta_o+xi_*[-d(h^2)], energy -1/6-integral h^3/3, and MA(U_N)=delta_o+delta_xi_N for every real N>0.
notes.text:
This is an unverified reconstructed foundation argument, not an incoming correctness grant.

Retain K=C((s)), |s|=exp(-1/8), t=s^8 and X=(G_m^2)^an/<(t,2),(3,t)>. For x_j=-log|z_j|, deck translations act on x by Z^2. Ordinary inverse images of rectangles of widths less than one have disjoint nonidentity translates and give quotient charts. On bounded tropical coordinate ranges only finitely many translation graphs occur; each graph is closed.

Conrad-Temkin, Non-archimedean analytification of algebraic spaces, author version 24 February 2009, Lemma 4.2.3 supplies quotient gluing over ordinary open covers. Lemma 4.2.4 supplies coherent G-sheaf descent for a flat quasi-finite surjection; its immediate proof reduces to finite faithfully flat affinoid algebras. Apply this to a FINITE disjoint union Z of injective quotient charts covering the compact tropical fundamental square, and to Z times Z->X times X. Each fibre is bounded by the number of charts. The pulled-back diagonal is a finite union of closed translation graphs with its evident coherent-ideal cocycle. Descent makes the quotient diagonal closed. Do not apply quasi-finite descent to the infinite-sheeted torus->X map.

The strict compact polyannulus x^{-1}([0,1]^2) surjects onto X. Centers in (1/8 Z)^2 and nested rectangles of widths 1/2 and 3/4 provide strict affinoid neighborhoods. Torus charts give smoothness, dimension two and empty boundary. Compactness, separation and empty boundary give properness. The torus has a connected polyannular exhaustion. Thus X is good, strict, smooth, separated, proper, boundaryless and connected of dimension two.

The Picard argument retains the exact Gruson boundary. Gruson 1968, IV.5 Theorem 1 gives SK^0(H)=0 for finite completed tensor products of disc algebras T_{1,r}, with r in the rationalized value group, and pure unit circles. For rank-one projective P, stable equality [P]=[H] and determinant cancellation trivialize P. No wide annulus occurs in that source theorem.

Induct on wide annulus factors. A line bundle on A(r,R) times Y is trivial on C(r) times Y by the lower-induction case. Glue it there to the trivial bundle on D(r) times Y. The finite rational G-cover D(r),A(r,R) of D(R) has intersection C(r): its inequalities are |z/a|<=1 and |a/z|<=1, with |a|=r and (a,z) the unit ideal. Coherent finite-cover descent, Van der Put GAU J7 (1975-76), 2.14-2.16.3, yields the filled bundle on D(R) times Y, which is trivial by induction. Thus products of the required discs, circles and wide annuli have Picard group zero. Deeper Tate/Kiehl descent remains published background.

For a unit sum b_beta z^beta on P_m={|s|^m<=|z_j|<=|s|^{-m}}, its Gauss log norm and the inverse's are convex and sum to zero, so are affine. A maximizing monomial at an interior point agrees with that affine function throughout the box. Hence the unit is b_alpha z^alpha(1+g), with zero constant coefficient and ||g||_{P_j}<=|s|^(m-j), j<m. A global torus unit is a scalar monomial, since another exponent would dominate on a ray. Normalize consecutive line-bundle frames by scalar monomials so e_{m+1}|P_m=(1+g_m)e_m. The products p_j=product_{m=j}^infinity(1+g_m)|P_j converge to units, with inverse tails converging. The frames e_j p_j glue on the interior exhaustion. Therefore Pic((G_m^2)^an)=0.

Commuting deck multipliers c_i z^{h_i}, with h_1=(A,B),h_2=(C,D), require t^C2^D=3^At^B. Valuations give C=B; prime factorization gives A=D=0. Thus h_1=(0,k),h_2=(k,0). If k!=0, choose n=(1,sign k), lambda=lambda(n), h=(kn_2,kn_1), so Q=v(lambda^h)=2|k|>0. A nonzero Laurent coefficient obeys
 a_{m+jh}=a_m c^j lambda^{-jm-hj(j+1)/2}.
Its valuation has negative quadratic leading term -Qj(j+1)/2, contradicting convergence on the unit polyannulus. If k=0, two distinct exponents cannot pair equally with both period valuations. Every nonzero section is consequently one nowhere-zero monomial.

For a local meromorphic fraction F=g/h, its intrinsic pole ideal J={b:bF is analytic} is the coherent kernel of multiplication by g into O/(h). Regular affinoid localizations are UFDs, by Stacks 0AG0, so cancellation makes J locally invertible. Flat restriction and coherent descent glue these ideals; Stacks 031T gives the normal height-one cancellation check. A global frame of its pullback to the torus gives analytic f_0 and f_1=Ff_0 with common deck multipliers. The recurrence makes their ratio constant. Thus Gamma(X,M)=K, without asserting a general analytic fraction equalizer.

Suppose X were the analytification of a separated finite-type K-algebraic space Y. Conrad-Temkin 2.3.1/2.3.2 reflect smoothness and dimension; clopen components analytify, and regular irreducible components are disjoint. Hence Y is integral and smooth of dimension two. Stacks 086U gives a dense scheme locus for a decent space. The exact hypotheses of 0ENA/0END/0EN6 hold: no embedded weak associates on regular noetherian etale charts, finite component conditions 0BB1, and generic field monomorphisms from separatedness/decency. Therefore global meromorphic functions identify with K(Y), of transcendence degree two. Coherent analytification and Ducros, Families of Berkovich spaces, 2.1.4 give regular, hence flat, algebraic-to-analytic local maps on the scheme charts. Flatness preserves nonzerodivisors, so rational functions analytify meromorphically. A closed point in a scheme open avoiding their zeros detects nonzero rational functions. Thus K(Y) injects into Gamma(X,M)=K, a contradiction.

The complete applied primary statements and immediate units were read. Deeper Berkovich descent and Ducros 2009/1993 regularity inputs remain named published foundations, not newly recursively audited proofs. All book contexts were not wholly freshly read. Accordingly this is a reconstructed proof under those foundations, not certification of the unrestricted source audit.

For the analytic formulas put q=(x_1^2+x_2^2)/2 and theta=DD q. Deck changes are affine. The identity-torus calibration has degree one and saturated lattice Z^2, giving theta^2=2 i_*dx for probability Haar measure dx. Raw mass is two. Periodically extend G(a)=a^2/2-a/2+1/12 and set u0=-G(x_1)-G(x_2), A=alpha_{u0}. Convex convolution gives A^2=2delta_o and theta wedge A=i_*(da tensor delta_0+delta_0 tensor da), with o=i(0). Mean G is zero, G(0)=1/12 and min G=-1/24. On F=tau^{-1}(0), u0=-1/6; E(u0)=-1/6 and sup u0=1/12.

On the ordinary sheet |x_j|<1/4 write w_j=z_j-1 and W={|w_j|<1}. Let R=-log max(|w_1|,|w_2|) on W and zero outside; R=infinity only at y=(1,1). For every real N>0 set D_N=-min(N,R), ell_j=log max(exp(-N),|w_j|), b_j=log max(1,|z_j|). Then
q+u0+D_N=max(ell_1+b_2,b_1+ell_2)-(1/2)log|z_1z_2|-1/6.
This is convex in ordinary unit moments. Near coordinate zeros omit inactive capped terms. Softmax gives ordinary smooth-positive local approximants. Thus U_N=u0+D_N lies in precisely C_theta. Theta and A vanish on W, while D_N vanishes off W, so D_N theta=D_N A=0.

For finite h=sum a_j 1_[0,N_j), with a_j>=0, increasing real N_j>0 and c=sum a_j<=1, put g=integral h and u_h=u0-g(R). Convex combinations give bounded membership. On W the local convex weight is sum a_j max(-N_j,y_1,y_2). Its softmax Hessian is a strictly positive covariance for c>0. Its gradient is a diffeomorphism onto p_1,p_2>0,p_1+p_2<c: strict convexity gives injectivity, and coercivity of softmax minus p dot y for interior p gives surjectivity. Uniform approximation error is at most epsilon c log 3. If h(N_j)<p_1+p_2<h(N_j-), inverse gradient points converge to the unique limiting minimizer (-N_j,-N_j). Exceptional slope boundaries have area zero. Changing variables in 2 det Hess gives mass h(N_j-)^2-h(N_j)^2 at the actual translated Gauss point xi_Nj. Composing arbitrary continuous analytic tests with the continuous degree-one Gauss section proves analytic weak convergence, including the exterior factor two. Affine or one-moment regions have zero top mass.

The outside atom is at o. Where exactly one |w_j|<1 the weights depend on at most one moment. Where all four z_1,w_1,z_2,w_2 have norm one, use their common moment. CLD-v2 8.8.6 and 12.2.7-10 locate top products on its two-dimensional tropical skeleton. The essential local dimension input was read directly: Ducros 2012, Espaces de Berkovich, polytopes, squelettes et theorie des modeles, Theorem 3.4, DOI 10.1142/S1793744212500077. For a Gamma-strict space and invertible local coordinates, its stabilized tropical germ has dimension at most their graded residual transcendence degree, with pure equality at boundaryless germs. Our strict charts permit Gamma={1}. Dependent reductions of z_1,z_2 give degree at most one. Independent reductions force every Laurent polynomial to have its unit Gauss norm, identifying o. The theorem's whole immediate proof was read; its deeper Theorem 1.3 and Temkin foundations remain explicit published inputs.

Conservation of mass now proves
MA(u_h)=(2-c^2)delta_o+xi_*[-d(h^2)].
The three energy integrals are respectively 0, -1/6 and -1/3-integral h^3. The first uses mean zero, the second D theta=D A=0, and the third u0=-1/6 on F and Tonelli integral g[-d(h^2)]=integral h^3. Therefore E(u_h)=-1/6-(1/3)integral h^3. In particular MA(U_N)=delta_o+delta_xi_N for every real N>0.

Complete artifacts: n2.md, P16.7-bounded-dual-paper.tex, proof-companion.md and source-application-ledger.md. Source copies/pixels remain under sources-LOCALONLY. Rerun python identity_audit.py and python diagnostics.py. Execution checks identities and finite formulas, not this foundation's mathematical correctness.

notes.summary: New exact FULL bounded dual 1/6+(2/3)integral h^3 for every genuine finite-energy continuous/discrete radial solution measure. Includes genuine nonpluripolar clamps; uniqueness remains radial only.
notes.detailedSummary: For right-continuous nonincreasing 0<=h<=1 constant on [0,1), with integral h^3 finite, genuine analytic products give (2-c^2)delta_o+xi_*[-d(h^2)] and mixed branch measure -d(hk). Explicit clamps handle endpoint atoms and prove nonpluripolar full mass without a rigid atom. Radial segment variation, variable-constant decreasing continuity, comparison and separated compactness are established. The bounded tangent inequality applies to every C_theta competitor and gives the full dual upper bound; Tonelli and bounded approximants give equality. Arbitrary Radon depth measures of branch mass <=1 and L^(3/2) tail are solved, including an unbounded example. No full intrinsic E1 recognition or ambient uniqueness is claimed.
notes.text:
Use the reconstructed bounded calculus and actual quotient/calibration in n1-n2. This is an unverified scoped proof.

Let H consist of right-continuous nonincreasing h with 0<=h<=1, constant c on [0,1), and Z(h)=integral_0^infinity h^3<infinity. Put g_h(r)=integral_0^r h and u_h=u0-g_h(R), with its canonical value at R=infinity. Then h tends to zero. Let nu_h=-d(h^2), a positive Stieltjes measure on [1,infinity), including any jump at 1. Its mass is c^2 and nu_h((t,infinity))=h(t)^2 for t>=1.

We prove
MA(u_h)=(2-c^2)delta_o+xi_*nu_h=:mu_h,
B(u_h,u_k)=(2-cd)delta_o+xi_*[-d(hk)],
E(u_h+C)=-1/6-Z(h)/3+2C,
sup_{v in C_theta}(E(v)-integral v mu_h)=1/6+2Z(h)/3.
The operator is genuinely constructed analytically; the final supremum is over the ENTIRE bounded class.

Choose compact finite steps h_m from below, retaining c on [0,1), sampling h at right endpoints on nested dyadic partitions of [1,2^m), and setting zero afterward. These increase to h. Their primitives increase to g_h uniformly on each finite depth interval. Thus u_m decrease to u_h locally uniformly off y. Depth is bounded on any compact subset off y: the closed bidiscs {R>=r} decrease to {y}, and compactness excludes intersection with all of them.

The local weight on W minus y is phi(max(log|w_1|,log|w_2|))-1/6, where phi(a)=-g_h(-a). Its derivative h(-a) is nonnegative and nondecreasing, so phi is convex nondecreasing. Ordinary unit-moment convex approximation proves local bounded membership; omit a zero inactive coordinate. Outside W the open {R<1} has u_h=u0+cD_1. Thus the local bounded operator already exists everywhere off y, independently of any inverse measure assignment.

The actual bounded measures mu_m=(2-c^2)delta_o+xi_*[-d(h_m^2)] converge weakly to the displayed mu_h. Indeed Stieltjes convergence holds on finite depth intervals; at a continuity depth r their tails are uniformly bounded by h(r)^2, tending to zero. Finite partition approximation followed by tail removal proves convergence against bounded continuous depth tests, hence against every continuous analytic test composed with xi. The pushforward is Radon because compact depth intervals have compact images and the finite measure is tight. Local product continuity off y identifies the limit with the actual local product. There is no atom or escaped mass at y, and total mass is two. Polarizing finite formulas and applying the same local convergence and tail argument gives the mixed formula, with positive branch measure -d(hk), branch mass cd and outside mass 2-cd.

The nonpluripolar recipe requires exact endpoint treatment. For M>0, if g_h(infinity)<=M the potential is bounded and the primitives converge uniformly globally, yielding its genuine bounded measure. If M<g_h(infinity), there is a unique finite positive r_M with g_h(r_M)=M. A plateau below the final value is impossible: a nonnegative nonincreasing derivative that reaches zero remains zero. Let h^M=h on t<r_M and zero on t>=r_M. Then
u^M=u0-min(g_h(R),M)=max(u_h,u0-M)
belongs to C_theta by finite real-cutoff approximation and the same convex moment presentation. This remains true if r_M<1; n2 proves every positive real cutoff. Near y the potential is exactly u0-M.

Its branch measure is nu_h below r_M, with the ENTIRE endpoint atom replaced by h(r_M-)^2 delta_rM, including any original endpoint jump. If r_M<1 this mass is c^2. The outside mass stays 2-c^2. On the strict set {g_h(R)<M}={R<r_M}, the whole clamp atom is excluded; locality gives
1_{g_h(R)<M}MA(nu^M)=1_{g_h(R)<M}mu_h.
As M increases, these restricted measures increase to mu_h off y. When g_h(infinity)=infinity the omitted tail h(r_M-)^2 tends to zero. The bounded case is already covered. This proves genuine nonpluripolar full mass two. For sufficiently large j, max(u_h+C,-j) is precisely the same clamp with M=j+C-1/6, since u0=-1/6 on W and the outside potential is bounded. Thus ordinary constant truncations give the same recipe. Clamping both mixed slots and restricting to their common strict unclamped set gives the mixed product; its omitted tail is bounded by h(r)k(r), tending to zero. No rigid atom occurs.

The first energy integral is integral u_h theta^2=0. The second is integral u_h theta alpha_{u_h}=-1/6, since the radial difference annihilates theta and A. These reference measures avoid the singular point. Tonelli gives, without infinity cancellation,
integral g_k(t)nu_h(dt)=integral_0^infinity k(t)h(t)^2dt.
Consequently the top integral is -1/3-Z(h), and the energy is -1/6-Z(h)/3. Constants add twice their value. These are genuine three-term energy integrals and bounded-energy limits.

For every h,k in H, Holder gives integral k h^2<=||k||_3||h||_3^2. Along h_t=(1-t)h+tk and C_t=(1-t)C+tD,
d/dt E(u_{h_t}+C_t)=-integral(k-h)h_t^2+2(D-C)
=integral[(u_k+D)-(u_h+C)]mu_{h_t},
d^2/dt^2 E(u_{h_t}+C_t)=-2integral(k-h)^2h_t<=0.
The undefined difference of infinite values at y is assigned zero on this null singleton. These prove all radial segment variations, concavity and order-monotonicity of energy.

For variable-constant decreasing continuity suppose u_{h_m}+C_m decreases and its energies are bounded below. A fixed point outside F shows C_m decreases. Since E_m<=-1/6+2C_m, it decreases to finite C. Put delta_m=C_m-C. The functions g_m-delta_m increase, are uniformly 1-Lipschitz and concave, and converge locally uniformly to a finite concave primitive g with g(0)=0 and constant derivative on [0,1). Concave secant inequalities give derivative convergence almost everywhere to h. The energy bound bounds Z_m, so Fatou gives Z(h)<infinity. Canonical values at infinity agree because sup_m sup_r(g_m(r)-delta_m)=sup_r sup_m(g_m(r)-delta_m).

Order gives g_m<=g+delta_m. Stieltjes integration by parts for every nonnegative nonincreasing compact test a yields
integral a h_m<=integral a h+delta_m a(0).
Take a=h_m^2 1_[0,L) and let L increase. Holder gives
Z_m<=Z(h)^(1/3)Z_m^(2/3)+delta_m.
Together with boundedness this forces limsup Z_m<=Z(h), while Fatou gives the opposite liminf. Thus energies converge, including variable constants. The estimate r h_m(r)^3<=Z_m gives uniformly vanishing squared tails; Stieltjes convergence therefore gives weak MA continuity and, with the product-tail bound, mixed continuity. This is radial continuity, not an all-direction theorem.

For radial comparison with variable constants put f=g_h-g_k and b=C-D. Inside W the strict comparison set is {f>b}; outside W it is present exactly when b<0. On each component interval (a,l) with positive contact endpoints, right and left derivative signs give h(a)-k(a)>=0 and h(l-)-k(l-)<=0. The difference of branch masses on that OPEN interval is
[h(a)^2-k(a)^2]-[h(l-)^2-k(l-)^2]>=0.
An infinite right endpoint has zero tails. For an initial interval and b=0 the same initial sign applies. For b<0 the initial c^2-d^2 is cancelled exactly by the included outside mass difference d^2-c^2. For b>0 there is no initial interval. Summing proves mu_k{u_h+C<u_k+D}<=mu_h{u_h+C<u_k+D}. Open endpoints exclude their atoms; y has zero mass.

Normalized radial energy sublevels Z<=L, C=0, are compact for uniform primitive convergence on finite intervals. Concave nondecreasing 1-Lipschitz primitives vanishing at zero have diagonal compactness; secant convergence and Fatou preserve Z<=L. Right-continuous derivatives give the limiting profile. This topology is metrizable and separated, equivalent to locally uniform convergence on compact subsets off y. Compact Gauss depth segments detect every primitive; the canonical value at y is determined, although evaluation there need not be continuous. All these potentials have sup=1/12, attained outside F.

Every positive Radon depth measure nu on [1,infinity), of mass c^2<=1 and with integral_1^infinity nu((t,infinity))^(3/2)dt finite, has a genuine radial solution: take h=c initially and h(t)=sqrt(nu((t,infinity))) afterward. Then -d(h^2)=nu, including its atom at 1. The energy condition is exactly Z=c^3+integral_1^infinity nu((t,infinity))^(3/2). Tails recover h, giving uniqueness modulo constants WITHIN the radial class. The branch bound is a restriction of this image family, not a universal cap.

Now establish the new FULL bounded dual. For the genuine finite-step u_m, n1 applies to EVERY v in C_theta:
E(v)-integral v mu_m<=E(u_m)-integral u_m mu_m=1/6+(2/3)Z(h_m).
Here integral u_m mu_m=-1/3-Z(h_m). Weak convergence against continuous v and Z(h_m) increasing to Z(h) give the upper bound 1/6+2Z(h)/3 over the ENTIRE class. Conversely test u_m against the actual limiting measure. Tonelli gives integral u_m mu_h=-1/3-integral h_m h^2, hence
E(u_m)-integral u_m mu_h=1/6-Z(h_m)/3+integral h_m h^2
->1/6+2Z(h)/3.
Monotone convergence supplies the limit. Thus the full bounded dual is exactly that finite value for EVERY constructed finite-energy continuous or discrete radial solution measure. For bounded profiles the solution itself attains it; for unbounded profiles bounded optimizing approximants suffice. If Z is infinite, the same lower tests diverge, excluding finite-energy eligibility.

For h=1 on [0,N) and zero afterward, mu=delta_o+delta_xi_N has full bounded dual 1/6+2N/3. The distinct 2delta_xi_N still has only the restricted lower bound 1/6+5N/3; its full admissibility and equation remain unresolved.

An explicit genuinely unbounded example is h=1/i on [i-1,i), i>=1. Its primitive diverges harmonically, while Z=sum_i 1/i^3 is finite. The actual measure is delta_o+sum_i(1/i^2-1/(i+1)^2)delta_xi_i, with telescoping branch mass one, full raw mass two and no rigid atom. Its full bounded dual is 1/6+(2/3)sum_i 1/i^3.

Bounded dual finiteness here is not an unproved recognition theorem for intrinsic all-direction E1, and radial uniqueness is not full uniqueness. Complete artifacts are n3.md, P16.7-bounded-dual-paper.tex and proof-companion.md. This is a scoped unverified paper, not a solution of literal original P16.7.

Independently reconstruct ROOT384's restricted-dual distinction. Let mu have raw mass two at actual branch points xi_N, N>=1, and T(t)=mu{xi_N:N>t}. For finite nonincreasing 0<=h<=1, compactly supported and constant initially, n2 and Tonelli give
E(u_h)-integral u_h mu=1/6+integral[hT-h^3/3].
Pointwise maximization over 0<=a<=1 gives a=min(1,sqrt(T)), with value Phi(T)=(2/3)T^(3/2) for T<=1 and T-1/3 for T>=1. This optimizer is nonincreasing. Finite truncations and nested step approximants converge monotonically in the objective, because T-a^2>=0 below the optimizer. Therefore the exact finite-combination radial restricted dual is 1/6+integral Phi(T), finite exactly when the tail belongs to L^(3/2).

For the smaller pencil u0+aD_N, put A(N)=integral_0^N T. Its optimized objective is 1/6+(2/3)A(N)^(3/2)/N^(1/2) when A(N)<=N, and 1/6+A(N)-N/3 otherwise. Since T tends to zero, A(N)/N tends to zero. Thus pencil finiteness is equivalent to sup_N A(N)/N^(1/3)<infinity. The inequalities NT(N)<=A(N) and integral_1^N t^(-2/3)dt=3(N^(1/3)-1) identify this with T(N)<=C N^(-2/3).

For N_i=2^i and masses 2(1-2^(-beta))2^(-beta i), i>=0, beta=2/3, the actual countable analytic measure has total mass two and tail comparable to t^(-2/3). It passes the pencil test, but every dyadic interval contributes a fixed positive amount to integral T^(3/2). Its radial restricted dual, hence its full bounded dual, is infinite. It is excluded by energy admissibility and cannot be an eligible original counterexample. For beta>2/3 restricted finiteness alone still does not prove full bounded admissibility for this total-branch-mass-two family.

For 2delta_xi_N0 the restricted optimizer is h=1 on [0,N0), giving exactly 1/6+5N0/3. This remains only a LOWER bound on the full C_theta dual. The genuinely solved delta_o+delta_xi_N0 in n3 has a different exact FULL value, 1/6+2N0/3. No universal atom cap follows from the chosen radial family's branch bound.

The positivity correction is also independent. Sym^2(Lambda^2 R^4) has dimension 21. Strong generators ww^T have decomposable w, whose Plucker coordinates (x,y) satisfy x dot y=0. A quadratic form vanishing on all such vectors has zero pure x and pure y terms. Its cross term x^TBy vanishes whenever x is perpendicular to y, forcing B^Tx parallel to x for every x. Basis vectors and pairwise sums force B scalar. Thus the annihilator is one-dimensional and the strong span is 20-dimensional. The middle PSD cone spans the full symmetric coefficient space and has an identity order unit; that is the convention used in n1. Arbitrary continuous multiplication is not asserted to preserve closedness.
